title: SK Hynix's US$299 billion chip plan faces military base hurdle
source_used: THE ELEC (Korea Electronics Industry Media) for the military-base angle, Reuters (via KFGO, 9 Oct 2026) for the visit and the plan's size; the Digitimes original is subscription-only
key_facts: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won visited Gwangju Military Airport and the surrounding ammunition depot on 9 Oct 2026 with SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung; it was his first visit.
Chey said construction could start with piling even if power and water are delayed; he could not say when, and an announcement could come soon.
The return of facilities used by US forces at the airport is seen as the biggest variable for the schedule; under the Status of Forces Agreement those areas must be returned before fabs can be built.
The handover timing and conditions will be set in South Korea-US negotiations; past US base returns in Korea took about a decade (Camp Long in Wonju 9 years, Yongsan to Pyeongtaek 13 years).

President Lee Jae Myung ordered the airport's military functions moved to another airport by mid-2028 and on 29 Sep asked officials to bring that forward; about one year and eight months remain to the planned start of construction.

On 6 Oct a People Power Party lawmaker asked at a parliamentary audit whether US forces would fully withdraw in time; Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said it was possible, gave no specifics, and later said the US was unlikely to reject the proposal.

Reuters (9 Oct): Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each plan to invest about 400 trillion won ($298.15 billion) for two fabs apiece in the Gwangju cluster, about 8.26 million square metres on the airport site and a neighbouring ammunition depot; the Gwangju plan is about two-thirds the size of Yongin.
quote_evidence: The return of facilities used by US forces at Gwangju Military Airport is seen as the biggest variable affecting the schedule.
Those areas must be returned before fabs can be built on the site.
Past cases show that returning US military bases can take about a decade.
why_it_matters_hint: A delay in handing back US-used areas could push back new memory capacity, but no date has been set and the foreign minister said the US was unlikely to refuse.
event_date: Chey visit 9 Oct 2026; THE ELEC article 11 Oct 2026; Digitimes 12 Oct 2026
notes: Digitimes (the pool item) is subscription-only; THE ELEC carries the same hurdle angle and was read in full. Reuters (9 Oct 2026) supplies the 400 trillion won (about US$298 billion) figure; Digitimes' headline gives US$299 billion for SK Hynix's plan. The Reuters piece was in the 9 Oct pool but not in a report edition.
